His first, Doing a Dyson, was written by James and also Tony Muranka in 1996, and was promptly followed by his first autobiography, Against the Odds, in 1997. James has long been a keen advocate of the importance of engineering education, and established the James Dyson Foundation in 2002, to inspire more young people to pursue careers in engineering and science.
